formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature, the USDC allowance that the owner (the signer) gives the spender is set to `value`. This replaces any earlier allowance.
The spender can then move up to `value` USDC from the signer with transferFrom until the allowance is used up.
The signer's permit nonce goes up by one, so earlier signatures with the same nonce stop working.
The signature works only until `deadline`. A deadline of type(uint256).max means it never expires.
formats.shown: The screen says "Authorize spending of tokens". It shows the spender as a raw address, the amount in USDC ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), a "Valid until" date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit shows the spender as a raw hex address with no name lookup.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, Permit format, field `spender`: "format": "raw". EIP2612._permit: _approve(owner, spender, value). This is the registry's usual ERC-2612 pattern, which the severity guide counts as a convention.
findings.fix: Change `spender` to "format": "addressName" with types ["contract","eoa"] and sources ["local","ens"].

findings.title: Permit deadline uint256 max means 'no expiry' but renders as a far-future date.
findings.evidence: EIP2612.sol _permit: require(deadline == type(uint256).max || deadline >= now, ...). descriptor.json field `deadline`: "format": "date", "encoding": "timestamp". It has no special-value handling. This is the registry's usual "Valid until" field.
findings.fix: If the spec allows a threshold or message on the date format, use it to show type(uint256).max as "No expiry".

findings.title: Permit intent is generic: it does not name USDC or the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", interpolatedIntent absent. The token and spender appear only in the fields.
